title: Shortlist
$comment: What the model is allowed to return. Note what is NOT here: no title, no platforms, no year, no genres. The catalogue already holds all of those and the model is never asked for a value the system already has — asking invites it to be wrong about a fact we could have looked up. The id is the join. Note also what is not bounded: the length of `case`. A numeric limit in a prompt is a request rather than a constraint (pitfall 15), and a schema that rejects a 121-word case costs two calls to discover a style preference. Length guidance lives in the prompt, unenforced, on purpose.

picks.$comment: Three normally. Fewer only when the candidate set held fewer — criterion 5 says a thin result is reported, never padded. The prompt states how many to return for the set it was given; this bound only stops a runaway.

id.$comment: Must appear in the candidate set that was sent. The schema cannot express that; src/shortlist.js checks it. Criterion 2.

angle.$comment: Must be an angle id from data/angles.json, and must not repeat within one shortlist. Checked in code against the pinned file rather than enumerated here, so adding an angle is one file rather than two. Criterion 6.

case.$comment: The argument for playing this game. Only a floor, and a low one: an empty or one-word case is a failure of the task rather than a style question, which is the distinction pitfall 15 draws.
